lessons.prompt:

Use attached first image (AIF) primarily for dimensional visual quality, text proportion and professional teaching polish; use second image only for technical clarity and dark palette. Do NOT copy their subject matter, people, grids or numbering. More AIF dimensional illustrative storytelling, fewer AIP outline boxes and no repeated glossy three-card rows. A calm midnight-navy #020d20 ground, white support text, cyan title key phrase, modest orange connectors, blue/violet service objects, subtle local lighting. Crisp labels, thin arrows, meaningful objects; no neon text, toy cartoon people, giant glowing panels, fake AWS marks or blank icon boxes. Title ~62px, premise ~34px, support ~32px. Title "CUSTOM BROKER: VERIFY, SCOPE, ISSUE".
Premise "A trusted backend verifies the employee's local identity, then requests a scoped AWS role session."
Create a central connected architecture story on open navy, with soft dimensional office/workstation at left representing "Employee app"; a modest central secure backend tower labeled "Trusted identity broker"; separate directory server below it labeled "Existing corporate identity system"; a compact AWS STS service object upper right, and Amazon S3 storage object lower right. No enclosing VPC or misleading hosting boundary.
Precise routing: Employee app → broker "Request AWS access"; broker ↔ directory labelled "Verify existing sign-in" (small two clearly directional lines if needed); broker side has a small linked checklist "Map trusted identity to an approved IAM role". Broker → AWS STS "AssumeRole • signed AWS request". AWS STS → broker "Temporary role credentials". Broker → Employee app "Return scoped credentials over TLS". Separate lower route Employee app → Amazon S3 "Signed request using temporary credentials"; S3 → employee app "Response". Never send STS credentials directly to directory, no client-to-STS shortcut in this broker example.
Compact credential object close to STS return explains "Access key ID + secret access key + session token". Show broker IAM authorization check near its STS call: "Broker may assume only approved roles." Near resource "Role policies limit actions and resources."
Two concise teaching annotations integrated into open space, not automatic footer bars: "The client cannot choose arbitrary privileges." and "Use standard federation when it meets the requirement; build a broker for a specific integration gap."
Illustration must teach responsibility and credential handoff, not decorate. No runnable JSON, no console screenshot, no misleading recommendation to embed permanent keys in the app. Balanced readable composition, retain explanatory depth without dense paragraphs.

lessons.title: SAML signature failure: check the trust
lessons.prompt:
Create one AWS Security course teaching image, 2048x1152, 16:9, refined AIF-leaning trial within VISUAL_STANDARD=AIP_AIF_SECURITY_BLEND_V1. Reference1 AIF defines professional 3D object rendering, navy palette and readable white/cyan typography; reference2 custom broker defines the current trial's technical polish, NOT its layout. Give this diagnostic topic its own composition. Less AIP panel framing; more integrated realistic dimensional documents, keys, laptop and repair mechanism. NO platforms/pedestals under objects this time, no generic three-card grid, no repeated person, no neon bloom or fake AWS logos. Near-black navy #020d20, white support ~32px, compact title ~62px, premise ~34px, selective orange, cyan and violet/blue technical objects. Exact small top marker "AWS SECURITY • FEDERATION TROUBLESHOOTING", top-right "19". Do not display any other header or style instructions.
Title "SAML SIGNATURE FAILURE: CHECK THE TRUST".
Premise "After a signing-key change, stale IAM provider metadata can prevent AWS from validating the SAML response."
Teaching layout: a dimensional laptop at left shows a modest dark diagnostic display with exactly two lines "InvalidIdentityToken" and "Response signature invalid". Label this area "Observed failure". Main visual center/right is a large but modest pair of signature/certificate objects connected by a broken verification link: left document is "Current IdP assertion" with attached key "Signed with Key B"; right certificate document is "IAM SAML provider metadata" with attached key "Still trusts Key A". Red small broken-link symbol between them and label "Signature cannot be verified in this example". A slim contextual label above "Worked case: IdP signing-key rotation". Key A and Key B are illustrative names, not actual certificate data. No corporate personal information.
Lower half is a focused four-action repair path, objects on the navy field without cards: "Get current IdP metadata" → "Update IAM SAML provider" → "Retry with a fresh assertion" → "Verify the expected role session". Small document/download, IAM trust certificate, replay arrow, verified session objects; clear compact action explanations respectively "Confirm the intended issuer"; "Refresh the signing-key information"; "Do not reuse the old response"; "Then test required access". At IAM update step show the exact CLI operation name only "aws iam update-saml-provider", not fabricated runnable command or flags.
Add an integrated concise note near repair path "Changing S3 permissions will not repair an invalid signature." Another separate short note "Use evidence to confirm this cause; not every federation failure is a signing-key mismatch." Avoid claiming certificate-date expiry alone automatically blocks IAM SAML authentication. No fake console walkthrough; this is diagnostic teaching. Do not omit causal relation, validation step or exact error. Keep all text readable, balanced proportions, fine connectors and substantial teaching information.

lessons.qa: Verified precise error text and CLI operation name; key-rotation example is a possible cause, metadata is refreshed from intended issuer, fresh assertion/retest precedes role and resource verification. lessons.title: Signed in but no account access: trace provisioning and assignment
lessons.layout: successful sign-in versus missing membership diagnostic
lessons.body: Small header "AWS SECURITY • WORKFORCE IDENTITY", top-right "21". Title "SIGNED IN, BUT NO ACCOUNT ACCESS?". Premise "Successful SAML sign-in does not create missing users, group memberships or account assignments." A dimensional employee browser on left shows "Sign-in successful" with a small green check, then an AWS access portal window at center-left shows "Expected account not visible". These are illustrative screens, not exact AWS console screenshots. Above: external corporate IdP → IAM Identity Center has two clearly distinct lanes: "SAML: authenticate sign-in" and "SCIM: provision users + groups". Add a small note "Manual provisioning is also supported." Focus right and lower on evidence-driven diagnosis, not a repeated overview: a connected inspection path with three compact evidence objects. First "Identity match" with exact meaningful check "SAML NameID matches provisioned username"; second "Group membership" with worked example "IdP: Alice in Analysts" / "Identity Center: membership missing"; third "Account assignment" with worked example "Analysts + ReadOnly + Analytics account". Mark the membership step as the failing case, other two as checks to confirm, not conclusively guaranteed. Show repair from missing membership to "Restore intended provisioning" → "Confirm membership and assignment" → "Refresh session and retest account access". Explain clearly "SAML does not query the IdP for users and groups." And "Do not add broad permissions to hide a provisioning fault." Use polished blue identity documents, teal membership links, violet IdP/IdentityCenter objects and an orange narrow diagnostic connector. Keep no passwords, actual company data, exact IAM code, fake AWS logos or giant framed dashboard. Richer color and modest gloss on objects, labels flat and sharp.

lessons.title: Permission sets provision scoped roles in assigned accounts
lessons.layout: one permission template provisions target-account roles
lessons.body: Header "AWS SECURITY • ACCOUNT ACCESS", exact top-right "22". Title "PERMISSION SET TO ACCOUNT ROLE". Premise "An account assignment connects a user or group, a permission set and a target AWS account." Open architecture: above left modest polished group object "Analysts"; center dimensional policy blueprint "ReadOnly permission set" inside a small logical "IAM Identity Center • organization instance" grouping, not a VPC or runtime host. Two clearly drawn target-account boundaries on right/lower, "Analytics account" and "Reporting account". A visible assignment annotation "Analysts + ReadOnly + target account" connects the group/template to each selected account. Within each account, show "Identity Center-managed IAM role" with attached policy document labeled "Policies from permission set". Precise arrow from permission-set configuration to each role labeled "Provision". Separate user session arrows from a modest AWS access portal browser to one target role, labeled "Select assigned account + role", then short arrow role session→account resources "Temporary role session". Do not draw permanent credentials or direct group→resource without role. Notes integrated naturally: "A permission set is a reusable policy template." "The role lives in the target account." "Review and reprovision permission-set changes to assigned accounts." "Other applicable policies and explicit Deny still apply." Keep visual mechanism more prominent than prose. Vibrant teal groups, sapphire/violet policy blueprint, green target accounts, orange configuration connectors; mild glossy materials only on objects. No automatic three equal panels or huge glass boxes.

lessons.title: Customer managed policy references need matching name and path in every account
lessons.layout: two account policy-reference outcomes and repair deployment
lessons.body: Header "AWS SECURITY • PERMISSION SET POLICIES", exact top-right "23". Title "POLICY REFERENCE: MATCH NAME AND PATH". Premise "A permission set references a customer managed policy; it does not copy that policy into member accounts." A polished central permission-set blueprint labeled "Customer policy reference" with exact simple evidence "Name: AppRead" and "Path: /team/". Two outgoing reference connectors to clearly separate account zones: Account A includes a dimensional IAM policy document "AppRead • /team/" with small check "Policy found"; Account B initially shows an empty document silhouette labeled "Policy missing" with red error "Provisioning fails". Make missing policy diagnostic distinct from runtime AccessDenied. A separate lower corrective path deploys policy to Account B: "Prepare policy in target accounts" → "Use StackSets or deployment automation" → "Retry permission-set provisioning". At lower-right small versioned documents A and B teach "Same name and path do not prove identical policy contents." Supporting note "Maintain equivalent policy versions when consistent access is required." Never claim AWS automatically duplicates customer managed policy JSON or that policy content must be identical for the reference to resolve. No runnable JSON. Rich green success / muted coral missing evidence, blue/violet objects with modest gloss; retain white/cyan crisp labels and thin connectors. Comparative evidence fits topic, no oversized decorative prop.

lessons.title: Identity Center attributes become trusted session tags for ABAC
lessons.layout: trusted identity attribute to session tag and two resource condition tests
lessons.body: Header "AWS SECURITY • ATTRIBUTE-BASED ACCESS", exact top-right "24". Title "ABAC: CARRY TRUSTED ATTRIBUTES INTO THE SESSION". Premise "IAM Identity Center can pass configured workforce attributes as session tags for policy evaluation." Left small trusted identity record "Department = Finance", supplied by "Configured identity source". Clear flow to "Identity Center attribute mapping" → "Role session" with exact tag label "aws:PrincipalTag/Department = Finance". Right two realistic compact EC2 compute instances within an AWS account: Finance instance tag "Department = Finance" and HR instance tag "Department = HR". A policy inspector for the worked action "ec2:StartInstances" explains in plain text "Match the session's Department to the instance's Department tag". Two separate condition outcomes: Finance "Matches this condition"; HR "Does not match this condition". Do NOT label matches as an unconditional ALLOW or non-match as an explicit Deny. Short precise small semantic key label "ec2:ResourceTag/Department" near resource tags, no invented JSON. Notes integrated: "A policy must grant the action using the condition; tags alone grant nothing." "Protect both identity attributes and resource-tag changes." "All other applicable authorization checks still apply." Use polished teal identity document, violet mapping object, sapphire credential/session object, green/coral small resource tags, restrained orange branching. No user-self-selected department or customer app roles. No literal reusable three-card layout. Keep exact long keys legible without tiny type.

lessons.title: Delegated administration keeps management-account controls separate
lessons.layout: organization control boundary and scoped member-account administration
lessons.body: Header "AWS SECURITY • WORKFORCE GOVERNANCE", exact top-right "25". Title "DELEGATED ADMIN: SCOPE THE CONTROL". Premise "An organization instance stays in the management account while a registered member account handles delegated administration." Main architecture within outer label "AWS Organizations": Management account upper-left contains "IAM Identity Center organization instance". Security member account lower-left contains "Delegated administrator" with modest workstation and admin shield. Development/Production member account groups right are clear simple containers, each shows "Permission sets + assignments". Arrow management→Security member labeled "Register delegated administrator". Arrow Security admin→Identity Center labeled "Authorized administration", then configuration connectors to member-account assignments. A crisp boundary note beside management account "Management-account permission sets stay under management-account administration." Small separate restricted-action list: "Cannot delete the Identity Center configuration", "Cannot register or deregister delegated administrators", "Cannot manage permission sets provisioned in the management account". Explain "Delegation changes who administers the service; it does not move the instance." And "Limit identity-store writes and SCIM token issuance to prevent unintended privilege changes." No false prerequisite claiming you must create a permission set/user assignment before registering delegation. No SCP protection claim for management account. Rich orange control marker, violet IdentityCenter, sapphire/teal member accounts, modest metallic gloss, flat quiet label areas. No fake console screenshot or walls of text.

lessons.title: Choose the directory boundary and account for Simple AD availability
lessons.layout: directory ownership decision with proxy path and legacy compatibility note
lessons.body: Header "AWS SECURITY • DIRECTORY SERVICES", exact top-right "26". Title "DIRECTORY CHOICES: WHO HOLDS THE DIRECTORY?". Premise "Choose a native managed directory or a proxy to an existing directory based on the required ownership boundary." Upper two meaningful architecture choices, not generic feature cards. LEFT: native AWS Managed Microsoft AD, dimensional Windows-like directory servers but no fabricated Microsoft logo; small AWS VPC logical boundary contains application and Managed Microsoft AD nodes, across two labeled AZs as a high-level availability sketch. Text "Actual Microsoft AD, operated by AWS" and "Supports directory trusts and AD-aware workloads". Do not pretend a VPC hosts the Identity Center service. RIGHT: AD Connector inside AWS VPC, a supported AWS app request passes through it over "VPN / Direct Connect" to separate "Existing self-managed AD" on-premises server. Clear opposite response arrow. Text "Directory gateway / proxy", "No directory-data replication or caching", "Network and on-premises AD remain dependencies". Lower compact legacy note with a smaller Samba-style generic directory object, not a third equal choice: "Simple AD: Samba-based AD-compatible directory". Status "Closed to new customers; existing customers retain functionality and can create directories." Explain briefly "For new deployments, evaluate Managed Microsoft AD or AD Connector." End with a useful concise choice cue "Native directory features → Managed Microsoft AD • Existing directory through a gateway → AD Connector". No outdated recommendation to select Simple AD for a new customer, no quota/pricing numbers, no unqualified native AD-equivalence for Simple AD. Glossy blue native directory, teal proxy links, violet existing directory, muted amber legacy tag. Preserve AIF dimensional polish, restrained framing, readable white/cyan typography and colorful teaching objects.

lessons.title: Hybrid directory trust and replication preserve different boundaries
lessons.layout: trust direction, hybrid dependencies and EC2 replica responsibility
